terms.definition: The neural network architecture introduced in this paper. It maps one sequence to another using attention layers and feed-forward layers, with no recurrence or convolution.
A two-part model design. The encoder turns the input sequence into internal vectors, and the decoder generates the output sequence from them.
A neural network operation that applies the same small learned filter to each local window of the input. In sequence models it combines each position with its nearby neighbours.
A mechanism that lets a model compute an output as a weighted combination of many inputs. The weights reflect how relevant each input is to what is currently being computed.
A widely used type of recurrent neural network whose gates control what information is kept or forgotten from step to step.
A type of recurrent neural network similar to the LSTM, but with a simpler gating design.
A neural network that processes a sequence one position at a time and carries a running internal state from each step to the next.
The internal vector a recurrent network carries from one step to the next. It summarizes what the network has read so far.
A processor with many cores that run calculations in parallel. It is the standard hardware for training neural networks.
A group of training examples that are processed together in one training step.
An earlier translation model built from convolutional layers instead of recurrent ones.
Attention in which the positions of a single sequence attend to each other, so the queries, keys and values all come from the same sequence.
A form of attention that runs several attention operations, called heads, side by side and then combines their outputs.
A model that converts one sequence into another, for example a sentence in one language into a sentence in another.
A training problem in which the learning signal shrinks towards zero as it passes back through many steps or layers. This makes long-range patterns hard to learn.
The basic units a text is split into before a model processes it. A token may be a word or a piece of a word.
Generating a sequence one element at a time, where each new element is conditioned on the elements already generated.
A shortcut that adds a layer's input to its output. It helps signals and gradients pass through deep networks.
An operation that rescales the components of each vector to a standard mean and spread, with learned adjustments. It helps keep training stable.
A learned vector that represents a discrete item, such as a token, so that the network can work with it numerically.
In attention, the vector for the position that is looking for relevant information. It is compared against the keys.
In attention, the vectors that queries are compared with. A key's match with the query decides how much weight its value receives.
In attention, the vector attached to each key. The attention output is a weighted sum of the values.
A score for two vectors, computed by multiplying them component by component and summing the results. It is larger when the vectors point in similar directions.
A function that turns a list of scores into positive weights that sum to 1. Higher scores receive larger weights.
An earlier form of attention that scores how well a query matches a key using a small neural network, rather than a dot product.
The number of dimensions of the query and key vectors in attention.
The derivatives that tell training how to adjust each parameter to reduce the error. If they are small, learning is slow.
A small two-layer neural network applied separately, with the same weights, to the vector at every position.
The paper's shorthand for the position-wise feed-forward sub-layer in each encoder and decoder layer.
An activation function that keeps positive inputs unchanged and sets negative inputs to zero.
A vector added to each token's embedding that records the token's position in the sequence.
A sine or cosine wave. Here, each dimension of the positional encoding follows such a wave with its own frequency.
The number of computation steps a signal must pass through in a network to connect two positions of a sequence.
A yearly shared evaluation for machine translation that publishes standard training and test datasets. The paper does not spell the acronym out.
Short for byte-pair encoding, a method that builds a vocabulary of common subword pieces by repeatedly merging frequent pairs of symbols.
Subword units from a word-piece vocabulary, which splits rare words into smaller, more frequent pieces.
A popular optimization algorithm that adapts the step size for each parameter using running averages of past gradients.
The size of the parameter updates made at each training step.
An initial phase of training in which the learning rate starts small and is gradually increased.
Techniques that discourage a model from fitting quirks of its training data, so that it performs better on new data.
A regularization method that randomly sets a fraction of a layer's outputs to zero during training.
A training technique that replaces the fully certain target for the correct token with a slightly softened one, spreading a little probability over the other tokens.
A measure of how well a model predicts the actual next tokens. Lower perplexity means the model assigns higher probability to what really comes next.
A standard automatic score for machine translation that measures how much a system's output overlaps with reference translations. Higher is better. The paper does not spell the acronym out.
Combinations of several separately trained models whose predictions are merged. They usually score better than any single member.
A standard set of news sentences from WMT 2014 that is used as the test set for translation.
A unit of computing speed. The paper uses it for the assumed throughput of each GPU.
A count of arithmetic operations on real numbers, used here as a measure of total training cost.
Copies of a model's parameters saved at points during training.
A decoding method that keeps the several most promising partial outputs at each step, instead of only the single best one.
An adjustment to beam search scores that controls how strongly shorter or longer outputs are favoured.
Held-out data used to tune settings and compare model variants. It is kept separate from the final test set.
When a model learns its training data so closely that it performs worse on new data.
The task of analysing a sentence into a tree of nested phrases, such as noun phrases and verb phrases.
A neural network that processes a sequence step by step while carrying a hidden state.
Describes models that map an input sequence to an output sequence, typically with an encoder and a decoder.
A large corpus of English sentences annotated by hand with their syntactic trees. It is the standard benchmark for parsing.
Training that combines a small set of hand-labelled data with a larger set of data whose labels were not produced by hand.
A score that combines precision and recall into a single number. For parsing, it measures how many predicted phrases match the correct tree.
The portion of the Penn Treebank made of Wall Street Journal text, used here for training and testing the parser.
Working out which earlier word or phrase a referring expression, such as a pronoun, points back to.
The earlier word or phrase that a pronoun or other referring expression refers to.
Experiments that remove or change one component of a model at a time to measure how much that component matters.
A later family of encoder-only Transformer models that are pretrained on large amounts of text.
A later family of decoder-only Transformer models that are trained to generate text one token at a time.
